program_name: Net Billing Tariff (NBT) - successor to net energy metering; IOUs brand it 'Solar Billing Plan'
incentive_structure: Hourly avoided-cost export credit (Avoided Cost Calculator values) + 9-yr ACC Plus adder for PG&E/SCE residential
event_limits: Applies to interconnection applications submitted on/after 2023-04-15; 9-year NBT legacy period for the original interconnecting customer; system sizing up to annual load +50% with attestation
tariff_schedule: CPUC D.22-12-056 (adopted 2022-12-15); implemented via Resolution E-5301 (2023-11-30)
on_peak_window: n/a - export credit is hourly, 8760 values per utility
peak_offpeak_rates: Import billed on a required 'electrification' TOU rate: E-ELEC (PG&E), TOU-D-PRIME (SCE), EV-TOU-5 (SDG&E)
export_compensation: Exports credited at CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator hourly values (usually below retail; can exceed retail on late-summer evenings); net surplus at true-up paid at wholesale (~$0.02-0.03/kWh)
stackable_with: NEM 2.0 legacy rules; SGIP; ELRP

program_name: Net Energy Metering 2.0 (legacy / grandfathered)
incentive_structure: Retail-rate bill credit for exports (import rates), netted per metered interval
event_limits: Closed to applications after 2023-04-14. 20-year legacy period from interconnection date (D.14-03-041); legacy runs with the system, not the owner. NEM 1.0 customers who rolled to NEM 2.0 do not get a second 20 years
peak_offpeak_rates: Exports credited at the customer's retail import rate
export_compensation: 1:1 retail-rate net metering, netted hourly (residential) / 15-min (non-res); non-bypassable charges on each net kWh consumed; net surplus at wholesale (~$0.02-0.03/kWh)
stackable_with: Storage may be paired with a NEM 2.0 system under D.14-05-033 / D.16-04-020 metering rules without losing legacy status

program_name: NEM legacy forfeiture threshold for system modifications (storage additions)
incentive_structure: Rule, not an incentive
event_limits: A grandfathered NEM 1.0/2.0 customer moves to the Solar Billing Plan at their next True-Up only if they increase the RENEWABLE GENERATING nameplate capacity by more than the greater of 1 kW or 10% of the original facility. Adding battery storage alone does not increase renewable generating nameplate capacity and therefore does not forfeit NEM legacy status. PG&E states this in its Solar Billing Plan FAQ.
export_compensation: Adding storage to a grandfathered NEM 2.0 system preserves NEM 2.0 export compensation; adding PV capacity above the 1 kW / 10% threshold forfeits it
stackable_with: NEM 2.0; SGIP

program_name: Solar Billing Plan (Schedule NBT)
incentive_structure: Hourly Energy Export Credit at ACC values, plus Energy Export Bonus Credit (ACC Plus adder) for residential systems receiving PTO before 2028
event_limits: Residential Energy Export Bonus Credit locked at PTO and paid for 9 years; available only to customers on the Solar Billing Plan before 2028. Business customers moved to SBP billing March 2026
on_peak_window: Required import rate: E-ELEC (Electric Home), peak 4-9 p.m. daily
export_compensation: Hourly Energy Export Credit set from CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator; 8760 hourly values published per year (2023-2026 sheets posted); + ACC Plus adder for residential pre-2028 adopters
stackable_with: SGIP; ELRP/Power Saver Rewards; SmartRate

program_name: Solar Billing Plan (Net Billing Tariff)
incentive_structure: Hourly export credit at ACC values, plus ACC Plus adder for residential systems interconnecting before end of 2027
event_limits: ACC Plus adder paid for 9 years; not available to customers required to install solar by building code
export_compensation: Hourly export credit at CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator values; + ACC Plus adder for residential pre-2028 adopters; net surplus at wholesale
stackable_with: SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

program_name: Solar Billing Plan (Net Billing Tariff)
incentive_structure: Hourly export credit at ACC values
event_limits: No ACC Plus adder - CPUC excluded SDG&E residential customers because SDG&E's higher retail rates already produce larger bill savings
export_compensation: Hourly export credit at CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator values; NO ACC Plus adder; net surplus at wholesale
stackable_with: SGIP; ELRP/Power Saver Rewards

program_name: Schedule E-ELEC - Residential Time-of-Use (Electric Home)
incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + daily income-tiered Base Services Charge
incentive_value_usd: Base Services Charge (eff 2026-03-01): $0.19713/day Income Tier 1, $0.39688/day Tier 2, $0.79343/day Tier 3. CA Climate Credit $36.18/household semiannual
event_limits: Mandatory rate for residential Net Billing Tariff customers. Otherwise requires a qualifying technology: EV, energy storage (>=2 kWh, or >=0.05% of annual kWh if usage >6,000 kWh/yr), or electric heat pump
tariff_schedule: Schedule E-ELEC (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61545-E; Advice 7975-E eff 2026-08-28; rates per Advice 7921-E eff 2026-06-01)
on_peak_window: Peak 4-9pm every day incl weekends/holidays; Part-peak 3-4pm and 9pm-12am; Off-peak all other hours. Summer = Jun 1-Sep 30
peak_offpeak_rates: Total bundled eff 2026-06-01: summer peak $0.55214 / part-peak $0.39026 / off-peak $0.33358 per kWh; winter peak $0.32063 / part-peak $0.29854 / off-peak $0.28468
export_compensation: Per Schedule NBT if on Solar Billing Plan; E-ELEC also open to legacy NEM/NEM2 customers with a qualifying technology
stackable_with: Solar Billing Plan (NBT); NEM/NEM2; SGIP; ELRP

program_name: Schedule E-TOU-C - Residential Time-of-Use (Peak Pricing 4-9 p.m. Every Day)
incentive_structure: TOU energy rate with baseline credit + daily income-tiered Base Services Charge
incentive_value_usd: Baseline credit $0.08140/kWh on baseline usage; Base Services Charge $0.19713 / $0.39688 / $0.79343 per day by income tier (eff 2026-03-01)
event_limits: Bill protection closed to customers enrolling after 2022-05-04
tariff_schedule: Schedule E-TOU-C (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61124-E, eff 2026-03-01; rates Advice 7921-E eff 2026-06-01)
on_peak_window: Peak 4-9pm all days year-round; Off-peak all other times. Summer = Jun 1-Sep 30
peak_offpeak_rates: Total bundled eff 2026-06-01: summer peak $0.52240 / off-peak $0.39940; winter peak $0.39757 / off-peak $0.36757 per kWh; less $0.08140/kWh baseline credit
export_compensation: Not a solar tariff by itself - export terms come from NEM2 or Schedule NBT
stackable_with: NEM2; SmartRate; SmartAC

program_name: Schedule EV2 (EV2-A) - Residential Time-of-Use for Plug-in Electric Vehicle Customers
incentive_structure: TOU energy rate with a very wide peak/off-peak spread + daily income-tiered Base Services Charge
incentive_value_usd: Base Services Charge $0.19713 / $0.39688 / $0.79343 per day by income tier (eff 2026-03-01)
event_limits: Storage-only enrollment is a PILOT capped at 30,000 storage-only customers; battery must be >=2 kWh (or >=0.05% of annual kWh above 6,000 kWh/yr). Whole-premise usage above 800% of baseline over 12 months forces removal to E-TOU-D and a 12-month ban from EV rates
tariff_schedule: Schedule EV2 (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61169-E eff 2026-03-01; rates Advice 7921-E eff 2026-06-01)
on_peak_window: Peak 4-9pm every day; Part-peak 3-4pm and 9pm-12am; Off-peak all other hours. Summer = Jun 1-Sep 30
peak_offpeak_rates: Total bundled eff 2026-06-01: summer peak $0.53809 / part-peak $0.42760 / off-peak $0.22558; winter peak $0.41099 / part-peak $0.39428 / off-peak $0.22558 per kWh
export_compensation: Not a solar tariff by itself; NEM2 customers may take EV2
stackable_with: NEM2; SGIP; ELRP

program_name: Schedule TOU-D Option 4-9PM (TOU-D-4-9PM)
incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + baseline credit + daily Base Services Charge
incentive_value_usd: Baseline credit $0.10/kWh up to monthly baseline allocation; Base Services Charge $0.79/day. Extra baseline allocation for heat-pump water heater customers (1.9 kWh/day summer, 2.6 kWh/day winter)
event_limits: Switching onto a TOU rate locks the customer out of another rate change for 12 months
on_peak_window: Summer (Jun-Sep): On-peak weekdays 4-9pm; weekend 4-9pm is Mid-peak; Off-peak all other. Winter (Oct-May): Super-off-peak 8am-4pm, Mid-peak 4-9pm, Off-peak all other
peak_offpeak_rates: Summer weekday on-peak 58c / off-peak 34c; summer weekend mid-peak 46c / off-peak 34c; winter mid-peak 51c / super-off-peak 33c / off-peak 37c per kWh (SCE-published rounded values, no effective date shown on page; subtract 10c baseline credit within allocation)
export_compensation: Per Schedule NBT or NEM2, depending on vintage
stackable_with: Solar Billing Plan; NEM2; SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

program_name: Schedule TOU-D Option 5-8PM (TOU-D-5-8PM)
incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + baseline credit + daily Base Services Charge
incentive_value_usd: Baseline credit $0.10/kWh up to monthly baseline allocation; Base Services Charge $0.79/day
event_limits: 12-month lock-in after a rate switch
on_peak_window: Summer (Jun-Sep): On-peak weekdays 5-8pm; weekend 5-8pm Mid-peak; Off-peak all other. Winter (Oct-May): Super-off-peak 8am-4pm, Mid-peak 5-8pm, Off-peak all other
peak_offpeak_rates: Summer weekday on-peak 74c / off-peak 34c; summer weekend mid-peak 54c / off-peak 34c; winter mid-peak 60c / super-off-peak 32c / off-peak 38c per kWh (SCE-published rounded values, no effective date shown on page)
stackable_with: NEM2; SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

program_name: Schedule TOU-D Option PRIME (TOU-D-PRIME)
incentive_structure: TOU energy rate with wide peak/off-peak spread + daily Base Services Charge; no baseline credit
incentive_value_usd: Base Services Charge $0.79/day; no baseline credit
event_limits: MANDATORY rate for SCE Solar Billing Plan (NBT) customers. Otherwise requires attestation of EV/PHEV ownership or lease, a residential battery, or an electric heat pump for water or space heating. 12-month lock-in after switching
on_peak_window: Summer (Jun-Sep): On-peak weekdays 4-9pm; weekend 4-9pm Mid-peak; Off-peak all other. Winter (Oct-May): Super-off-peak 8am-4pm, Mid-peak 4-9pm, Off-peak all other
peak_offpeak_rates: Summer weekday on-peak 59c / off-peak 26c; summer weekend mid-peak 40c / off-peak 26c; winter mid-peak 56c / super-off-peak 24c / off-peak 24c per kWh (SCE-published rounded values, no effective date shown on page)
export_compensation: Per Schedule NBT (hourly ACC export credit + ACC Plus adder)
stackable_with: Solar Billing Plan; SGIP; ELRP; Smart Energy Program

program_name: Schedule TOU-D Options A, B and T (discontinued TOU periods)
incentive_structure: Legacy TOU rate options
event_limits: Closed to new enrollment; existing customers may stay but cannot return once they leave
tariff_schedule: Schedule TOU-D Options A / B / T
on_peak_window: Legacy TOU periods (not the 4-9pm or 5-8pm structure)
stackable_with: NEM2

program_name: Schedule TOU-DR1 - Residential Time of Use Service
incentive_structure: TOU energy rate + baseline adjustment credit + daily Base Services Charge
incentive_value_usd: Baseline Adjustment Credit $0.10905/kWh up to 130% of baseline; Base Services Charge $0.79343/day standard, $0.39688/day for CARE(DRAH) and FERA (eff 2026-01-01)
event_limits: SDG&E states TOU-DR1 is its standard residential schedule
on_peak_window: On-Peak 4-9pm; Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak all other hours. Summer = Jun-Oct
peak_offpeak_rates: Total eff 2026-01-01: summer on-peak $0.69654 / off-peak $0.47560 / super-off-peak $0.38818; winter on-peak $0.62200 / off-peak $0.54019 / super-off-peak $0.44933 per kWh
export_compensation: Per NEM2 or Schedule NBT depending on vintage
stackable_with: NEM2; SGIP; ELRP

program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program (ELRP) - non-residential / Group A and Group B
incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment for measured load reduction; no penalty for non-performance
incentive_value_usd: $2.00/kWh for every kWh of measured voluntary reduction (non-residential)
event_limits: May-Oct, 7 days/wk, 4-9pm window; events 1 hr min to 5 hr max; up to 60 event-hours per year; consecutive days allowed. Triggered by CAISO EEA Watch/EEA-1/2/3 or (residential) a day-ahead Flex Alert
tariff_schedule: ELRP pilot per CPUC D.21-12-015 as updated by D.23-12-005
peak_offpeak_rates: n/a - event-based payment, not a rate
export_compensation: BTM solar+storage with permission to export explicitly eligible under Group A
stackable_with: Group B allows customers already in CAISO market-integrated DR (DRAM, CBP) to earn ELRP for INCREMENTAL reduction beyond what is committed to CAISO. Base Interruptible Program customers are eligible for Group A

program_name: Power Saver Rewards (residential ELRP sub-program A.6)
incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment for incremental load reduction during events
incentive_value_usd: $1.00/kWh for voluntary incremental residential load reduction
event_limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm; 1-5 hr events; 60 hr/yr program cap. Nearly 4 million IOU customers were auto-enrolled starting summer 2022
export_compensation: n/a - measured against a baseline, not an export tariff
stackable_with: Non-res ELRP; utility DR programs

program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program (PG&E, administered via Olivine)
incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment
incentive_value_usd: $2.00/kWh of measured load reduction (non-residential, per CPUC ELRP terms)
event_limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm, 1-5 hr events, 60 hr/yr cap
stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program (Group B, incremental only)

program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program (SCE)
incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment
incentive_value_usd: $2.00/kWh of measured load reduction (non-residential, per CPUC ELRP terms)
event_limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm, 1-5 hr events, 60 hr/yr cap
stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program (Group B, incremental only); Smart Energy Program

program_name: Emergency Load Reduction Program (SDG&E)
incentive_structure: $/kWh performance payment
incentive_value_usd: $2.00/kWh of measured load reduction (non-residential, per CPUC ELRP terms)
event_limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm, 1-5 hr events, 60 hr/yr cap
stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program (Group B, incremental only)

program_name: Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) - Residential Solar and Storage Equity (RSSE, AB 209 budget)
incentive_structure: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate + $/kW solar rebate
incentive_value_usd: Storage $1,100/kWh; Solar $3,100/kW (CPUC-published rate table, current as of 2026-09-16). Authorized budget $280 million
event_limits: Reservations opened 2025-06-02. Open to any low-income residential electric and/or gas customer in California (not only IOU customers). All applicants must enroll in a qualified Demand Response program within one year of reserving funds. CPUC D.24-03-071 established the budget; Resolution E-5362 opened it; Resolution E-5373 handles IRA tax-credit interaction
export_compensation: Rebate is upfront; export compensation comes from the customer's NEM/NBT tariff
stackable_with: NBT / Solar Billing Plan; ELRP; a qualified DR program is REQUIRED

program_name: SGIP - Small Residential Storage budget (general market)
incentive_structure: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
incentive_value_usd: $150/kWh (CPUC rate table)
event_limits: CPUC lists this budget as available through 2025. Requires enrollment in a qualified DR program within one year of reservation
stackable_with: NBT; ELRP

program_name: SGIP - Equity Resiliency budget
incentive_structure: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
incentive_value_usd: $1,000/kWh (CPUC rate table)
event_limits: CPUC lists this budget as available through 2025. Targeted at customers in high fire-threat districts, PSPS-affected areas and medical-baseline / vulnerable households. Established by D.19-09-027
stackable_with: NBT; ELRP

program_name: SGIP - San Joaquin Valley Residential budget
incentive_structure: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
incentive_value_usd: $1,100/kWh (CPUC rate table)
event_limits: PG&E or SCE residential customers only; CPUC lists as available through 2025
stackable_with: NBT; ELRP

program_name: SGIP - Non-Residential Equity and Large-Scale Storage budgets
incentive_structure: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
incentive_value_usd: Non-Residential Equity $850/kWh; Large-Scale Storage $250/kWh; SCE San Joaquin Valley Non-Residential $1,000/kWh; Generation $2,000/kW (CPUC rate table)
event_limits: IOU customers (PG&E, SCE, SDG&E, SoCalGas) including unbundled/CCA customers. CPUC lists these budgets as available through 2025
stackable_with: ELRP; Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program

program_name: Demand Side Grid Support (DSGS) Program
incentive_structure: Upfront capacity commitment payment plus per-unit net-load-reduction payment
event_limits: Events May through October during extreme grid events. Options 1-4; residential batteries participate via aggregators. Guidelines Fifth Edition adopted 2026; CEC issued a budget update notice 2025-10-01
peak_offpeak_rates: n/a - event payment, not a rate
stackable_with: Separate from and stackable in principle with CPUC ELRP; verify per-event double-counting rules with the administrator (Olivine)

program_name: Schedule E-BIP - Base Interruptible Program
incentive_structure: $/kW-month capacity payment on Potential Load Reduction, with $/kWh penalty for energy above Firm Service Level
incentive_value_usd: 15-Minute BIP: Nov-Apr $10.60 (1-500 kW) / $11.20 (501-1,000 kW) / $11.80 (>1,000 kW) per kW-month; May-Oct $13.60 / $14.20 / $14.80 per kW-month. 30-Minute BIP: Nov-Apr $9.50 / $10.00 / $10.50; May-Oct $12.50 / $13.00 / $13.50 per kW-month. Rates effective 2025-05-17 (Advice 7572-E); D.23-12-005 authorized the $2/kW May-Oct adder for 2024-2027. Excess Energy Charge $6.00/kWh above Firm Service Level ($8.40/kWh after a failed re-test)
event_limits: Max 1 event/day, 6 hours max per event, max 10 events/calendar month, 180 hours/calendar year; year-round; 15- or 30-minute notice. Two utility test events per year count as program events. Requires >=100 kW max demand and FSL <=85% of highest monthly max demand, minimum 100 kW reduction
tariff_schedule: Schedule E-BIP (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61454-E et seq.; Advice 7942-E eff 2026-07-10, Res. E-5451)
on_peak_window: Dispatch triggered by CAISO market award / Operating Procedure 4420, or PG&E T&D reliability need; measured against summer on-peak / winter on-peak or partial-peak demand
peak_offpeak_rates: n/a - capacity payment, not a rate
export_compensation: Customers on Net Energy Metering schedules (except NEMCCSF) are eligible
stackable_with: STACKS WITH: ELRP, Schedule E-SLRP, and (legacy dual enrollments only) Peak Day Pricing. PROHIBITED with any other capacity-based program including the Capacity Bidding Program

program_name: Underfrequency Relay (UFR) Program (rider to Schedule E-BIP)
incentive_structure: $/kW-month demand credit for automatic underfrequency interruption
incentive_value_usd: $0.67/kW-month demand credit on average monthly summer on-peak / winter partial-peak demand
event_limits: Automatic interruption when system frequency drops to 59.65 Hz for 20 cycles. Direct-enrolled customers only (not available through DR aggregators). PG&E may require up to 3 years written notice to terminate
tariff_schedule: Schedule E-BIP, Underfrequency Relay Program section
stackable_with: Base Interruptible Program

program_name: Demand Response Auction Mechanism (DRAM)
incentive_structure: Competitive auction for Resource Adequacy capacity from third-party DR aggregators bidding into CAISO
event_limits: Last delivery year was 2024. The CPUC issued its final decision in April 2024 to discontinue DRAM after the 2024 delivery year; the pilot ran from 2016 through 2024 via D.16-06-029, D.17-10-017 and D.19-07-009. Successor capacity-accreditation treatment for DR is being developed in the CPUC DR proceeding
tariff_schedule: DRAM pilot (CPUC DR proceeding; CAISO Proxy Demand Resource registration)
stackable_with: Superseded; aggregators now reach CAISO via the Proxy Demand Resource / DERP models and ELRP

program_name: Schedule E-CBP - Capacity Bidding Program
incentive_structure: Monthly $/kW capacity payment on nominated load plus $/kWh energy payment for delivered event curtailment; paid to the aggregator, who sets customer compensation
event_limits: Aggregator-managed and integrated into CAISO as a Proxy Demand Resource (PDR). Season May 1 - Oct 31. 'Elect' option: max 1 event/day, 4-hour max event duration, participant may elect more than 6 events/month. Day-ahead notification by 5 p.m. Triggered by a CAISO market award for the CBP PDR. NO minimum demand requirement. Net-metered, partial-standby, Auto-DR, bundled, DA and CCA customers eligible; full-standby, WAPA-served and NEMCCSF customers are not
tariff_schedule: Schedule E-CBP (Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 49623-E; Advice 6160-E, D.21-03-056)
on_peak_window: May 1 - Oct 31 event windows, day-ahead notice
stackable_with: May dual-participate with Schedule E-OBMC and with ELRP Group B (incremental reduction only). NOT compatible with the Base Interruptible Program (both are capacity-based)

program_name: Peak Day Pricing (PDP)
incentive_structure: Summer rate discount in exchange for a high event-day surcharge
event_limits: 9 to 15 Peak Day Pricing Event Days per year, typically the hottest summer days. New dual enrollment with the Base Interruptible Program has not been available since 2018-10-26
peak_offpeak_rates: Summer rates are discounted; effective rates are higher during PDP event hours (specific credit and surcharge values published in the underlying rate schedules, not on the program page)
stackable_with: Automated Demand Response; legacy BIP dual enrollment only

program_name: Schedule E-OBMC - Optional Binding Mandatory Curtailment Plan
incentive_structure: No cash incentive - the benefit is exemption from rotating outages; penalty-only structure
incentive_value_usd: $0 incentive; $6.00/kWh penalty for each kWh above the commitment
event_limits: Must reduce entire circuit load 5-15% within 15 minutes of alert (eligibility requires ability to achieve 15% below baseline). Events any day including weekends/holidays with no frequency or duration limit. Second failure in a 1-year period terminates the plan and bars re-entry for 5 years
on_peak_window: Any day, any hour, no cap
stackable_with: Capacity Bidding Program

program_name: Automated Demand Response (ADR) incentive
incentive_structure: Upfront $/kW incentive for OpenADR-capable automation, capped as a share of project cost
incentive_value_usd: $200/kW for approved projects, up to 75% of eligible project costs
event_limits: Requires enrollment in an eligible PG&E DR program (Peak Day Pricing or Capacity Bidding Program), OpenADR 2.0a/2.0b capability, 12 months billing history, and a 3-year (Standard option 1) or 5-year (option 2) participation commitment
stackable_with: REQUIRES co-enrollment in Peak Day Pricing or the Capacity Bidding Program

program_name: Automated Response Technology (ART)
incentive_structure: Incentive set and paid by the third-party ART provider, not by PG&E
event_limits: Events may occur at any time and last 1 to 4 hours in a single day; day-ahead email notification. Enrollment is via a third-party provider. Batteries may export stored energy to the grid during events
export_compensation: Battery may send energy to the grid during program events
stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with SmartRate, SmartAC, WatterSaver and other PG&E residential DR - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

program_name: SmartRate (residential critical peak pricing)
incentive_structure: Summer rate discount plus a high per-kWh surcharge during SmartRate event hours, with a first-year Bill Protection guarantee
event_limits: PG&E's page states SmartRate is 'risk free and backed by our Bill Protection guarantee'; the per-kWh credit and event surcharge are set in the underlying rate schedule and were not retrievable from the published tariff PDF path tested
stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with other PG&E residential DR programs - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

program_name: SmartAC
incentive_structure: Bill credit for utility-controlled A/C cycling via a SmartAC switch
event_limits: Requires a central air conditioning unit; PG&E remotely shifts A/C load out of peak hours
stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with other PG&E residential DR programs - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

program_name: WatterSaver
incentive_structure: Enrollment bonus plus monthly participation credit
incentive_value_usd: $50 gift card enrollment bonus plus $5 gift card credit for every month of participation
event_limits: Requires an electric water heater; heating is shifted automatically to lower-cost hours
on_peak_window: Shifts water heating out of high-price hours
stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with other PG&E residential DR programs - PG&E residential rule: a customer may participate in only ONE energy incentive / peak-hour / direct-bidding program at a time

program_name: Behind-the-Meter Optimization of Load Technology (BOLT) Study
incentive_structure: One-time enrollment bonus plus a post-participation reward, per device
incentive_value_usd: Behind-the-meter batteries up to $400 each; electric vehicles up to $125 each; smart thermostats up to $100 each. No device limit. Rewards paid in two stages (enrollment bonus, then after study participation)
event_limits: Study, not a permanent tariff. Enrollment through study partners EnergyHub, Octopus or Uplight/Optiwatt. EV participants must have home charging
tariff_schedule: Behind-the-Meter Optimization of Load Technology Study
stackable_with: Runs through third-party aggregators; interaction with Smart Energy Program / Summer Discount Plan not stated on SCE's page

program_name: Smart Energy Program (SEP)
incentive_structure: One-time sign-up bill credit plus annual bill credits for thermostat events
incentive_value_usd: $75 one-time sign-up credit plus up to $50/year in bill credits for maintaining enrollment June 1 - Sept 30
event_limits: Requires a qualifying smart thermostat with a central A/C system. SCE raises the thermostat setpoint up to 4 degrees during events; customer may override any event at any time
stackable_with: SCE states customers may be enrolled in only one A/C-based program at a time (SEP or Summer Discount Plan)

program_name: Summer Discount Plan (SDP)
incentive_structure: Monthly summer bill credits for utility-controlled A/C cycling
incentive_value_usd: Up to $160/year in summer bill credits
event_limits: Requires a central A/C system. SCE cycles the A/C off and on during events. The 'override' program option allows opting out of up to 5 events per year. Credits earned June 1 - Sept 30
stackable_with: Mutually exclusive with the Smart Energy Program

program_name: Capacity Bidding Program - Elect (CBP-E) and CBP-E Direct
incentive_structure: Capacity Payments plus Energy Payments; for CBP-E the aggregator sets what the customer receives
incentive_value_usd: Aggregator-determined for CBP-E; CBP-E Direct pays based on event performance
event_limits: Summer-only, event-based. CBP-E Direct credits earned May 1 - Oct 31. Open to all customer classes
